Stat. ch. 192-194; fee level, work days, comp rules, thresholds and economics are team assumptions to confirm before real filings. The uniformity basis carries Florida's assessment level: cautious market value x the county value-to-price ratio Find measures (cost-of-sale adjustment, s.193.011(8)).

llm.deskRulesText: Florida. Property is assessed at just (market) value as of January 1. A value petition (form DR-486) to the county Value Adjustment Board argues the January 1 just value is too high; it is due within 25 days after the county mails its TRIM notice, and each county sets its own date. Claim bases: market_value argues the January 1 just value is above market value; uniformity (here: Florida's assessment level) argues it is above market value times the county's typical value-to-sale-price ratio, which reflects the statutory cost-of-sale adjustment (Fla. Stat. 193.011(8)); the ratio is measured by Find on the county's own sales. Evidence is arm's-length sales of similar homes in the same neighborhood or building, time-adjusted to January 1. Homestead properties are capped (Save Our Homes), so a lower just value may not lower the tax bill; the savings figure already accounts for caps and exemptions. A representative filing for the owner needs the owner's signed authorization on the petition. Comparable distances are not measured: comps come from the subject's own neighborhood or building.
